role.en: Filipino painter and lawyer; honoured beside Juan Luna in Rizal's 1884 brindis
role.fil: Pilipinong pintor at abogado; pinarangalan katabi ni Juan Luna sa brindis ni Rizal noong 1884
role.de: Philippinischer Maler und Jurist; neben Juan Luna in Rizals Trinkspruch von 1884 geehrt

portrait.alt: Oil portrait of Félix Resurrección Hidalgo in a dark coat and white collar against an olive ground
portrait.credit: Tomas Bernardo, Portrait of Felix Resurrecion Hidalgo, 1958. National Museum of the Philippines

quote.en: In [Félix Resurreción] Hidalgo's painting beats the purest sentiment, the ideal expression of mournfulness, beauty and vulnerability, the victims of brute force, and it is because Hidalgo was born beneath the brilliant azure of that sky, the lullaby of its breezes, amid the serenity of its lakes, the poetry of its valleys and the majestic harmony of its hills and mountains.
quote.fil: Sa pintura ni [Félix Resurreción] Hidalgo ay tumitibok ang pinakadalisay na damdamin, ang huwarang pagpapahayag ng pighati, ng ganda at ng kahinaan, ang mga biktima ng mabangis na lakas, at ito ay sapagkat isinilang si Hidalgo sa ilalim ng maningning na bughaw ng langit na iyon, ng oyayi ng mga simoy nito, sa gitna ng katahimikan ng mga lawa nito, ng tula ng mga lambak nito at ng maringal na pagkakatugma ng mga burol at bundok nito.
quote.de: In [Félix Resurreción] Hidalgos Malerei schlägt das reinste Gefühl, der ideale Ausdruck von Trauer, Schönheit und Verletzlichkeit, der Opfer roher Gewalt, und das kommt daher, dass Hidalgo unter dem strahlenden Azur jenes Himmels geboren wurde, dem Wiegenlied seiner Winde, inmitten der Stille seiner Seen, der Poesie seiner Täler und des majestätischen Einklangs seiner Hügel und Berge.

quoteSource.en: Rizal's brindis to F. R. Hidalgo and J. Luna, Madrid, 25 June 1884

bio.en:
Coming from a line of wealthy and gracious art patrons in Calle de la Escolta, Félix Eduardo Resurreción Hidalgo y Padilla was bound to be an artist. However, Hidalgo also belonged to a clan of well-known lawyers, which led him to pursue law at the University of Santo Tomas in 1867 upon completing his studies at the Ateneo. Proficiency in law proved to be in his blood, often receiving sobresaliente (excellent) marks as he earned his Bachelor in Law degree in 1871.

But this did not lose Hidalgo's passion for the arts. By 1876, he had exhibited at the Teatro Circo de Bilibid as a student of the Academia de Dibujo y Pintura. In the same year, Hidalgo caught Spain's attention for the Universal Exposition in Philadelphia, which debuted some of his works—La Banca, La Vendedora de Lanzones, and El Pescador de Sucag.

The Academia's director, Agustin Saez, was impressed by his work, which often received the mark of sobresaliente. He later bagged a scholarship in 1879 to take up art studies at the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando in Spain through an art contest. He then crossed paths with Rizal in Spain in 1883; he was taking painting courses at the same university while also studying at the College of Medicine and the College of Philosophy and Letters of the Universidad Central de Madrid. During this time, Hidalgo painted Rizal's portrait and sent it to his family in Calamba, Laguna.

Hidalgo, like Rizal, achieved international acclaim and received more than just praises in the art scene. His Las Jovenes Cristianas Expuestas al Populacho was part of the 1884 Exposición Nacional de Bellas Artes and gained ninth place out of 15 silver medals. He also bagged a silver award at the Exposition Universelle de Paris in 1889 for his La Barca de Aquente, side-by-side with Juan Luna's Hymen, oh Hyménéé, which won bronze. But among his artworks, the El Asesinato del Gobernador Bustamante showed Hidalgo's strong political inclination. This painting depicted a violent mob of friars who brutally killed Philippine Governor-General Fernando Bustamante, who ousted an archbishop protecting corrupt officials involved in the Manila Galleon Trade. The downfall of the cleric led to the corrupt officials' arrest. As such, this was symbolically linked with the three Filipino priests Mariano Gomez, José Burgos, and Jacinto Zamora (GOMBURZA) and the struggle of the ilustrados (or Enlightened, referring to Filipinos who were educated in Europe at that time). Declared a National Cultural Treasure (NCT) in 1974, it is now exhibited at the National Museum of Fine Arts in Manila, opposite the Spoliarium of Juan Luna.

Hidalgo and Rizal's common interest was not just art—it was their love for the motherland. Among Rizal's contemporaries, Hidalgo was one of those who received a copy of Noli Me Tangere hot off the press in 1887. Rizal requested feedback on his novel, which Hidalgo indulged him with:

“I have read the pages of your book and I have found them full of truth. There are scenes finely delineated with an absolutely remarkable exactness… I admire your courage in saying plainly what you think and the inspiration reflected in your work which makes one feel the palpitations of the heart of a man who loves his country…” — Hidalgo's comment on the Noli Me Tangere, shared in Rizal's letter to F. Blumentritt, 29 March 1887.
bio.fil:
Mula sa angkan ng mayayaman at magagandang-loob na tagatangkilik ng sining sa Calle de la Escolta, nakatadhana si Félix Eduardo Resurreción Hidalgo y Padilla na maging alagad ng sining. Gayunman, kabilang din si Hidalgo sa isang angkan ng kilalang mga abogado, na siyang umakay sa kanya upang mag-aral ng batas sa Unibersidad ng Santo Tomas noong 1867 matapos niyang tapusin ang kanyang pag-aaral sa Ateneo. Napatunayang nasa kanyang dugo ang husay sa batas, at madalas siyang tumanggap ng markang sobresaliente (napakahusay) habang tinatapos ang kanyang Bachelor in Law noong 1871.

Ngunit hindi nito napawi ang pagmamahal ni Hidalgo sa sining. Pagsapit ng 1876, nakapagtanghal na siya sa Teatro Circo de Bilibid bilang mag-aaral ng Academia de Dibujo y Pintura. Sa taon ding iyon, napansin ng Espanya si Hidalgo para sa Universal Exposition sa Philadelphia, kung saan unang ipinakita ang ilan sa kanyang mga akda—La Banca, La Vendedora de Lanzones, at El Pescador de Sucag.

Humanga ang direktor ng Academia na si Agustin Saez sa kanyang gawa, na madalas tumanggap ng markang sobresaliente. Nakamit niya noong 1879 ang isang iskolarship upang mag-aral ng sining sa Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando sa Espanya sa pamamagitan ng isang paligsahan sa sining. Nagkrus ang kanilang landas ni Rizal sa Espanya noong 1883; kumukuha siya ng mga kurso sa pagpipinta sa parehong unibersidad habang nag-aaral din sa College of Medicine at sa College of Philosophy and Letters ng Universidad Central de Madrid. Sa panahong ito, ipininta ni Hidalgo ang larawan ni Rizal at ipinadala ito sa pamilya nito sa Calamba, Laguna.

Tulad ni Rizal, nakamit ni Hidalgo ang pandaigdigang pagkilala at higit pa sa papuri sa mundo ng sining. Ang kanyang Las Jovenes Cristianas Expuestas al Populacho ay bahagi ng 1884 Exposición Nacional de Bellas Artes at umabot sa ikasiyam na puwesto sa 15 pilak na medalya. Nagwagi rin siya ng pilak sa Exposition Universelle de Paris noong 1889 para sa kanyang La Barca de Aquente, katabi ng Hymen, oh Hyménéé ni Juan Luna na nagwagi ng tanso. Ngunit sa kanyang mga akda, ang El Asesinato del Gobernador Bustamante ang nagpakita ng matinding hilig ni Hidalgo sa pulitika. Inilarawan ng pinturang ito ang marahas na pulutong ng mga prayle na buong-bangis na pumatay kay Gobernador-Heneral Fernando Bustamante, na nagpatalsik sa isang arsobispong nagtatanggol sa mga tiwaling opisyal na sangkot sa Kalakalang Galyon ng Maynila. Ang pagbagsak ng klerigo ay humantong sa pagkaaresto ng mga tiwaling opisyal. Dahil dito, simbolikong iniugnay ito sa tatlong paring Pilipino na sina Mariano Gomez, José Burgos, at Jacinto Zamora (GOMBURZA) at sa pakikibaka ng mga ilustrado (o mga Naliwanagan, tumutukoy sa mga Pilipinong nag-aral sa Europa noong panahong iyon). Idineklarang Pambansang Yamang Pangkalinangan (NCT) noong 1974, ito ay nakatanghal ngayon sa National Museum of Fine Arts sa Maynila, katapat ng Spoliarium ni Juan Luna.

Ang pinagsaluhang interes nina Hidalgo at Rizal ay hindi lamang sining—ito ay ang kanilang pag-ibig sa inang bayan. Sa mga kapanahon ni Rizal, si Hidalgo ay isa sa mga tumanggap ng sipi ng Noli Me Tangere kaagad matapos itong mailimbag noong 1887. Humingi si Rizal ng puna hinggil sa kanyang nobela, na ibinigay naman ni Hidalgo:

“Nabasa ko na ang mga pahina ng iyong aklat at natagpuan kong punô ang mga ito ng katotohanan. May mga tagpong pinong iginuhit nang may lubhang kahanga-hangang katumpakan… Hinahangaan ko ang iyong tapang sa tahasang pagsasabi ng iyong iniisip at ang inspirasyong masasalamin sa iyong akda na nagpapadama sa atin ng pintig ng puso ng isang taong nagmamahal sa kanyang bayan…” — Puna ni Hidalgo sa Noli Me Tangere, ibinahagi sa liham ni Rizal kay F. Blumentritt, 29 Marso 1887.
bio.de:
Aus einer Linie wohlhabender und großzügiger Kunstmäzene in der Calle de la Escolta stammend, war Félix Eduardo Resurreción Hidalgo y Padilla zum Künstler bestimmt. Hidalgo gehörte jedoch auch einer Sippe bekannter Juristen an, was ihn 1867 nach Abschluss seiner Studien am Ateneo zum Jurastudium an der Universidad de Santo Tomas führte. Die Begabung für das Recht lag ihm im Blut: Er erhielt häufig die Note sobresaliente (ausgezeichnet) und erwarb 1871 seinen Bachelor in Jura.

Doch das nahm Hidalgo nicht die Leidenschaft für die Kunst. Bis 1876 hatte er als Schüler der Academia de Dibujo y Pintura im Teatro Circo de Bilibid ausgestellt. Im selben Jahr erregte Hidalgo Spaniens Aufmerksamkeit für die Weltausstellung in Philadelphia, wo einige seiner Werke debütierten — La Banca, La Vendedora de Lanzones und El Pescador de Sucag.

Der Direktor der Academia, Agustin Saez, war von seiner Arbeit beeindruckt, die oft die Note sobresaliente erhielt. 1879 gewann er über einen Kunstwettbewerb ein Stipendium für ein Kunststudium an der Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando in Spanien. 1883 kreuzten sich in Spanien seine Wege mit denen Rizals; er belegte Malkurse an derselben Universität und studierte zugleich an der Medizinischen Fakultät sowie der Fakultät für Philosophie und Literatur der Universidad Central de Madrid. In dieser Zeit malte Hidalgo Rizals Porträt und sandte es dessen Familie in Calamba, Laguna.

Wie Rizal erlangte Hidalgo internationale Anerkennung und erhielt in der Kunstwelt mehr als bloßes Lob. Sein Las Jovenes Cristianas Expuestas al Populacho war Teil der Exposición Nacional de Bellas Artes von 1884 und belegte den neunten von 15 Plätzen mit Silbermedaille. Auf der Exposition Universelle de Paris von 1889 gewann er zudem Silber für sein La Barca de Aquente, Seite an Seite mit Juan Lunas Hymen, oh Hyménéé, das Bronze erhielt. Unter seinen Werken zeigte jedoch El Asesinato del Gobernador Bustamante Hidalgos ausgeprägte politische Haltung. Das Gemälde stellt einen gewalttätigen Mob von Mönchen dar, die Generalgouverneur Fernando Bustamante brutal töteten, nachdem dieser einen Erzbischof abgesetzt hatte, der korrupte, in den Manila-Galeonenhandel verwickelte Beamte schützte. Der Sturz des Klerikers führte zur Verhaftung der korrupten Beamten. So wurde das Werk symbolisch mit den drei philippinischen Priestern Mariano Gomez, José Burgos und Jacinto Zamora (GOMBURZA) und dem Kampf der ilustrados verknüpft (der „Aufgeklärten“, womit die damals in Europa ausgebildeten Filipinos gemeint sind). 1974 zum Nationalen Kulturschatz (NCT) erklärt, hängt es heute im National Museum of Fine Arts in Manila, gegenüber dem Spoliarium von Juan Luna.

Das gemeinsame Interesse von Hidalgo und Rizal war nicht nur die Kunst — es war ihre Liebe zum Vaterland. Unter Rizals Zeitgenossen gehörte Hidalgo zu denen, die 1887 druckfrisch ein Exemplar des Noli Me Tangere erhielten. Rizal bat um eine Rückmeldung zu seinem Roman, die Hidalgo ihm gewährte:

„Ich habe die Seiten Ihres Buches gelesen und sie voller Wahrheit gefunden. Es gibt Szenen, die mit einer durchaus bemerkenswerten Genauigkeit fein gezeichnet sind… Ich bewundere Ihren Mut, klar zu sagen, was Sie denken, und die Inspiration, die sich in Ihrem Werk spiegelt und einen die Schläge des Herzens eines Mannes spüren lässt, der sein Land liebt…“ — Hidalgos Kommentar zum Noli Me Tangere, mitgeteilt in Rizals Brief an F. Blumentritt, 29. März 1887.
